For metered US voice, our comparison of twelve providers puts the carriage itself at roughly $0.003 to $0.020 per minute depending on provider and direction, plus a small monthly fee for each phone number. That range is the reason SIP trunk prices are hard to quote: a premium retail provider and a wholesale carrier can differ by around twenty times for the same workload.
There are three ways to be billed for the voice carriage, and choosing between them matters more than shaving a fraction of a cent off the rate.
Per second or minute of voice carried

The same rate can cost very different amounts depending on the billing increment: the unit each call is rounded up to. Per-second billing charges for the actual duration. A 60-second increment rounds every call up to the next full minute. Our comparison notes that some carriers bill in 6-second or 60-second increments, and that this matters because AI calls are often short.

Premium retail providers charge for developer tooling, support, and features, while wholesale carriers sell bare minutes at lower rates but expect you to run more of the stack. Our 2026 comparison found around a twenty-times spread between the cheapest and the most expensive option for the same outbound workload.

No, not on its own. A trunk carries the call. The speech-to-text, language model, and text-to-speech are separate costs unless you use a bundled platform. Ringlyn bundles the telephony layer into its platform pricing, so you do not buy a trunk separately.
